claim:
For the equal-temperature two-mode squeezed thermal state \(\rho_{\mathrm{TMST}}(r,\beta)\) of Mishra--Morelli--Baksov\u00e1--Rembold--Friis and their optimized covariance-only fidelity witness with a two-mode squeezed-vacuum target, put \(u=\operatorname{coth}(\beta/2)\) and \(\beta_c=\log(2+\sqrt{3})\). The source quantity obeys the exact identity
\[
\widetilde R_{\mathrm{opt}}^2=\frac{u\cosh(2r)(u^2-1)}{u\cosh(2r)+\sqrt{1+u^2\sinh^2(2r)}}.
\]
Consequently, if \(0<\beta\le\beta_c\), then \(\widetilde R_{\mathrm{opt}}>1\) for every finite \(r\ge0\), so the source fidelity lower bound \(\widetilde F_{\mathrm{opt}}=[1-\min\{1,\widetilde R_{\mathrm{opt}}\}]^2\) vanishes identically and this fidelity-based covariance witness certifies only the trivial Schmidt-number lower bound \(1\), regardless of squeezing. In the same regime the entanglement-of-formation method applied to the same covariance matrix has
\[
\operatorname{SN}(\rho_{\mathrm{TMST}})\ge \exp h(ue^{-2r})\sim \frac{e}{4u}e^{2r},
\]
so arbitrarily large Schmidt number is nevertheless certifiable from the same second moments as \(r\to\infty\). If \(\beta>\beta_c\), then \(\widetilde R_{\mathrm{opt}}\to a_\beta=1/(\sqrt2\sinh(\beta/2))<1\), and the fidelity witness itself eventually certifies an exponentially growing Schmidt number. More precisely, for \(r>0\) and \(\widetilde F_{\mathrm{opt}}>0\), with \(s_{\mathrm{opt}}=\tfrac12\operatorname{arsinh}(u\sinh(2r))\), its certified lower bound is
\[
K_{\mathrm{fid}}=\max\!\left\{1,\left\lceil\frac{\log(1-\widetilde F_{\mathrm{opt}})}{\log(\tanh^2 s_{\mathrm{opt}})}\right\rceil\right\},
\]
and
\[
K_{\mathrm{fid}}\sim C_\beta e^{2r},\qquad C_\beta=\frac{u}{4}\Bigl[-\log\bigl(1-(1-a_\beta)^2\bigr)\Bigr].
\]
Thus \(\beta_c\) is an exact all-squeezing thermal threshold separating complete failure of this covariance-to-fidelity Schmidt-number certificate from exponential high-dimensional certification, while the same covariance data retain exponentially growing EoF-based certification on both sides of the threshold.

correctness.rationale: Starting from the anchor's exact Eqs. (50)--(52), the optimized target can be eliminated exactly. Rationalization gives a positive closed form whose denominator is strictly below twice its leading term, yielding a uniform-in-squeezing lower bound and the exact limiting value. The critical equation is solved exactly. The TMSV threshold in Eq. (53) is an elementary geometric sum, and the strict witness inequality gives the stated ceiling formula. The EoF asymptotic follows from the explicit function in Eq. (33). A standalone script checks the identities and asymptotic constants at representative parameters; the proof itself is analytic.
risks: The EoF asymptotic is used only in the large-squeezing regime where its argument tends to zero.
No numerical experiment is used to justify an infinite-parameter conclusion.

value.rationale: The paper motivates high-dimensional certification from easy second-moment measurements and directly compares several methods. The new theorem identifies an exact temperature at which one newly proposed conversion becomes completely powerless for all squeezing, while another certificate from the same covariance data still grows exponentially. Above the threshold it supplies the exact exponential growth coefficient of the fidelity certificate. This separates loss in the conversion theorem from loss in the measured data and gives a sharp design boundary for when that witness can or cannot certify high dimension.
risks: The threshold is method-specific and should not be interpreted as a physical entanglement transition.
The result does not optimize over arbitrary non-Gaussian target families or stronger moment-based witnesses.
